cues.en: So in hindsight, maybe Netflix should have based the Netflix prize on a metric that's more focused on top-n recommenders.
cues.zh: 事後看來，也許 Netflix Prize 應該根據更聚焦於 Top-N 推薦的指標來評比。

cues.en: It turns out there are a few of them.
cues.zh: 這類指標其實有好幾種。

cues.en: One is called hit rate, and it's really simple.
cues.zh: 其中一種叫做命中率，非常簡單。

cues.en: You generate top-n recommendations for all of the users in your test set.
cues.zh: 為測試集中的所有使用者，產生 Top-N 推薦。

cues.en: If one of the recommendations in a user's top-n recommendations is something they actually rated, you consider that a hit.
cues.zh: 如果某位使用者的 Top-N 推薦中，有一個是他實際評分過的項目，就算一次命中。

cues.en: You actually managed to show the users something that they found interesting enough to watch on their own already.
cues.zh: 你確實成功向使用者展示了他原本就感興趣、願意自行觀看的東西。

cues.en: So we'll consider that a success.
cues.zh: 所以把這視為成功。

cues.en: Just add up all of the hits and your top-n recommendations for every user in your test set, divide by the number of users and that's your hit rate.
cues.zh: 將測試集每位使用者的 Top-N 推薦中的命中次數加總，再除以使用者人數，就是命中率。

cues.en: Hit rate itself is easy to understand, but measuring it is a little bit tricky.
cues.zh: 命中率本身很容易理解，但衡量起來有點棘手。

cues.en: We can't use the same train test or cross validation approach we used for measuring accuracy because we're not measuring the accuracy on individual ratings.
cues.zh: 不能使用前面衡量準確程度的訓練／測試或交叉驗證方法，因為這裡不是衡量個別評分的準確程度。

cues.en: We're measuring the accuracy of top-n lists for individual users.
cues.zh: 而是衡量每位使用者的 Top-N 清單的準確程度。

cues.en: Now you could do the obvious thing and not split things up at all, and just measure hit rate directly on top-n recommendations created by a recommender system that was trained on all
cues.zh: 當然，可以用最直覺的方法，完全不切分資料，直接用全部資料訓練推薦系統，再衡量它產生的 Top-N 推薦

cues.en: of the data you have, but technically that's cheating.
cues.zh: 命中率；但嚴格來說，這是在作弊。

cues.en: You generally don't want to evaluate a system using data that it was trained with.
cues.zh: 一般不應該用系統訓練過的資料評估它。

cues.en: I mean, think about it.
cues.zh: 想想看。

cues.en: You could just recommend the actual top 10 movies rated by each user using the training data and achieve a hit rate of 100%.
cues.zh: 你只要根據訓練資料，推薦每位使用者實際評分最高的十部電影，就能達到 100% 命中率。

cues.en: So a clever way around this is called leave-one-out cross-validation.
cues.zh: 一種聰明的解決方法，叫做留一交叉驗證。

cues.en: What we do is compute the top-n recommendations for each user in our training data and intentionally remove one of those items from that user's training data.
cues.zh: 做法是，計算訓練資料中每位使用者的 Top-N 推薦，並刻意從該使用者的訓練資料中移除一個項目。

cues.en: We then test our recommender systems ability to recommend that item that was left out in the top-n results that creates for that user in the testing phase.
cues.zh: 接著在測試階段，檢查推薦系統為該使用者產生的 Top-N 結果，能否推薦出被移除的項目。

cues.en: So we measure our ability to recommend an item in a top-n list for each user that was left out from the training data.
cues.zh: 因此，我們衡量的是，對每位使用者，能否在 Top-N 清單中推薦出訓練資料刻意留下不用的項目。

cues.en: That's why it's called leave one out.
cues.zh: 所以叫做「留一」。

cues.en: The trouble is, it's a lot harder to get one specific movie right while testing, than to just get one of the n recommendations.
cues.zh: 問題是，測試時要猜中某一部特定電影，比只要猜中 N 個推薦中的任一個，困難得多。

cues.en: So hit rate with leave-one-out, tends to be very small and difficult to measure, unless you have very large data sets to work with.
cues.zh: 因此，搭配留一法的命中率通常非常小，很難衡量，除非有非常大的資料集。

cues.en: But it's a much more user-focused metric when you know your recommender system will be producing top-n lists in the real world, which most of them do.
cues.zh: 但如果知道推薦系統在真實世界會產生 Top-N 清單，而大多數系統都是如此，這就是更以使用者為中心的指標。

cues.en: A variation on hit rate is average reciprocal hit rate or ARHR for short.
cues.zh: 命中率有一種變形，叫做平均倒數命中率，簡稱 ARHR。

cues.en: This metric is just like hit rate, but it accounts for where in the top end list your hits appear.
cues.zh: 這個指標與命中率相同，但會考慮命中項目在 Top-N 清單中的位置。

cues.en: So you end up getting more credit for successfully recommending an item in the top slot than in the bottom slot.
cues.zh: 所以，成功推薦的項目出現在最前面，會比出現在最後面，得到更多分數。

cues.en: Again, this is a more user-focused metric since users tend to focus on the beginning of lists.
cues.zh: 這同樣更以使用者為中心，因為使用者通常注意清單前面的項目。

cues.en: The only difference is that instead of summing up the number of hits, we sum up the reciprocal rank of each hit.
cues.zh: 唯一差異是，不是加總命中次數，而是加總每次命中的排名倒數。

cues.en: So if we successfully predict a recommendation in slot three, that only counts as one third, but a hidden slot, one of our top-n recommendations receives the full weight of 1.0.
cues.zh: 因此，如果成功命中第三個位置，只算三分之一；但如果命中 Top-N 推薦的第一個位置，就能得到完整的 1.0 權重。

cues.en: Whether this metric makes sense for you depends a lot on how your top-n recommendations are displayed.
cues.zh: 這個指標適不適合你，很大程度取決於 Top-N 推薦如何顯示。

cues.en: If the user has to scroll or paginate to see the lower items in your top-n list, then it makes sense to penalize good recommendations that appear too low in the list, where the user has to work to find them.
cues.zh: 如果使用者必須捲動或換頁，才能看到清單下方的項目，那麼好的推薦如果排太低、得費力才能找到，給予懲罰就合理。

cues.en: Another twist is cumulative hit rate.
cues.zh: 另一種變形是累積命中率。

cues.en: Sounds fancy, but all it means is that we throw away hits if our predicted rating is below some threshold.
cues.zh: 聽起來很厲害，但意思只是，如果預測評分低於某個門檻，就不計那次命中。

cues.en: The idea is that we shouldn't get credit for recommending items to a user that we think won't actually enjoy.
cues.zh: 概念是，不應該因為推薦了我們認為使用者其實不會喜歡的項目，還獲得分數。

cues.en: An alternative approach, which is what we actually do in the code for this course, is to filter out recommendations based on the actual observed ratings in our test data.
cues.zh: 另一種做法，也是本課程程式碼實際採用的方法，是根據測試資料中實際觀察到的評分，過濾推薦。

cues.en: The idea there would be to not get credit for recommending items that we know users didn't like.
cues.zh: 概念是，推薦了已知使用者不喜歡的項目，不應該得到分數。

cues.en: So in this example, if we had a cutoff of three stars we throw away the hits for the second and fourth items in these test results and our hit rate metric wouldn't count them at all.
cues.zh: 因此這個例子中，如果以三顆星為門檻，就會移除測試結果中第二與第四個項目的命中，命中率指標完全不計算它們。

cues.en: Yet another way to look at hit rate is to break it down by predicted rating score.
cues.zh: 還有一種看待命中率的方式，是依預測評分拆開來看。

cues.en: It can be a good way to get an idea of the distribution of how good your algorithm thinks recommended movies are that actually get a hit.
cues.zh: 這能幫助了解，實際命中的推薦電影，在演算法眼中有多好，以及其分布。

cues.en: Ideally you want to recommend movies that they actually liked and breaking down the distribution gives you some sense of how well you're doing in more detail.
cues.zh: 理想上，你要推薦使用者實際喜歡的電影，拆解分布能更詳細了解表現。

cues.en: This is called a rating hit rate or RHR for short.
cues.zh: 這叫做評分命中率，簡稱 RHR。

cues.en: So those are all different ways to measure the effectiveness of top-n recommenders offline.
cues.zh: 以上都是離線衡量 Top-N 推薦成效的不同方式。

cues.en: The world of recommender systems would probably be a little bit different if Netflix awarded the Netflix prize on hit rate, instead of RMSC.
cues.zh: 如果 Netflix Prize 根據命中率，而不是 RMSE 頒獎，推薦系統領域可能會有些不同。

cues.en: It turns out that small improvements in RMSC can actually result in large improvements to hit rates which is what really matters.
cues.zh: 事實上，RMSE 小幅改善，就可能帶來命中率的大幅提升，而命中率才是真正重要的。

cues.en: But it also turns out that you can build recommender systems with great hit rates, but poor RMSC scores.
cues.zh: 但也可能建立命中率很棒、RMSE 分數卻不好的推薦系統。

cues.en: And we'll see some of those later in this course.
cues.zh: 本課程稍後會看到一些例子。

cues.en: So RMSC and hit rate aren't always related.
cues.zh: 所以，RMSE 和命中率不一定相關。
